s: alcohol, liquor (beverage containing the former substance)
Alkohol.et: Borrowed from Medieval Latin alcohol, ultimately from Arabic الكُحْل (al-kuḥl, “kohl”).

Alkali.et: From French alcali, ultimately from Arabic اَلْقِلْي (al-qily, “alkali, ashes of the saltwort”).

s: alcove, particularly: a bed built or let into the wall
Alkoven.et: From French alcôve f, from Spanish alcoba, from Arabic القبَة. The later final -n and masculine gender in German through association with unrelated Middle Low German koven (“stable, shed, nook”).

s: a municipality of Upper Austria, Austria

s: auk, any bird of the family Alcidae
Alk.et: Borrowed from Swedish alka (used scientifically by Carl von Linné), from Old Norse alka, from Proto-Germanic *alkǭ.
